req.title: Basic-auth handles special characters
req.statement: The system shall URL-decode <user> and <passwd> path segments before comparing against the supplied Basic credentials.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that /basic-auth/<user>/<passwd> must URL-decode path segments before comparing against Basic credentials. Tests must cover: (1) positive path with URL-encoded special characters that decode to valid credentials, (2) negative path where credentials do not match the URL-decoded path segments, (3) boundary cases with percent-encoded characters at the edge of valid encoding (e.g., %40 for @, %3A for colon, %2F for slash). The check_basic_auth function compares auth.username == user and auth.password == passwd, where user/passwd come from the Flask route (already URL-decoded by Werkzeug). We must assert exact status codes (200 vs 401) and exact JSON payload fields to kill comparison-mutation and constant-mutation operators.

tests.name: test_basic_auth_special_chars_at_sign_positive
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
URL path contains %40 (encoded @) in user segment
Basic credentials match the decoded user/passwd
actions: Send GET /basic-auth/user%40example.com/p%40ss with Authorization: Basic base64(user@example.com:p@ss)
tests.executable:
import base64
from httpbin.core import app

client = app.test_client()

credentials = base64.b64encode(b'user@example.com:p@ss').decode('ascii')
headers = {'Authorization': f'Basic {credentials}'}
r = client.get('/basic-auth/user%40example.com/p%40ss', headers=headers)
assert r.status_code == 200
data = r.get_json()
assert data['authenticated'] == True
assert data['user'] == 'user@example.com'

def test_basic_auth_special_chars_at_sign_positive():
    client = app.test_client()
    credentials = base64.b64encode(b'user@example.com:p@ss').decode('ascii')
    headers = {'Authorization': f'Basic {credentials}'}
    r = client.get('/basic-auth/user%40example.com/p%40ss', headers=headers)
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert data['authenticated'] == True
    assert data['user'] == 'user@example.com'

tests.name: test_basic_auth_correct_user_wrong_encoded_passwd_negative
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
URL path has encoded special char in passwd
Credentials supply the raw (non-decoded) percent-encoded string as password
actions: Send GET /basic-auth/bob/p%40ss with Authorization: Basic base64(bob:p%40ss) — literal percent-encoded string, not decoded
expected: HTTP 401 response — credentials do not match because path decodes to p@ss but supplied password is literal p%40ss
tests.executable:
import base64
from httpbin.core import app

def test_basic_auth_correct_user_wrong_encoded_passwd_negative():
    client = app.test_client()
    # Supply the literal percent-encoded string as password (not decoded)
    credentials = base64.b64encode(b'bob:p%40ss').decode('ascii')
    headers = {'Authorization': f'Basic {credentials}'}
    r = client.get('/basic-auth/bob/p%40ss', headers=headers)
    # Path decodes to p@ss, but credential has p%40ss — must be 401
    assert r.status_code == 401

test_basic_auth_correct_user_wrong_encoded_passwd_negative()
